pages.title: A – C
pages.body:
- **Ad hoc network:** Devices connected directly to each other without a router.
- **Asimov’s laws:** Three fictional rules for robot behaviour (1942).
- **Binary:** The base-2 number system using 0 and 1.
- **Bitcoin:** A decentralised digital currency created in 2009.
- **Blockchain:** A shared ledger of linked blocks of transactions.
- **Blog:** A website of posts displayed newest first.
- **Cashless society:** A society in which most payments are electronic.
- **Cloud storage:** Saving data on remote servers accessed through the Internet.
- **Cyberbullying:** Repeated harassment of a person using digital technology.

pages.title: C – H
pages.body:
- **Cyberstalking:** Persistent online monitoring or threatening of a person.
- **DDoS:** Distributed Denial of Service: flooding a server with traffic.
- **Device driver:** Software that lets the OS communicate with a device.
- **Digital footprint:** The trail of data a person creates online.
- **Digital shadow:** Data about a person created or collected by others.
- **E-commerce:** Buying and selling over electronic networks.
- **E-paper:** A reflective display technology that looks like ink on paper.
- **Expert system:** A program that imitates a human expert using rules.
- **Hexadecimal:** The base-16 number system using 0–9 and A–F.

pages.title: H – P
pages.body:
- **Holographic storage:** Storage using laser light to record data in three dimensions.
- **IDE:** Integrated Development Environment for writing and debugging code.
- **Inference engine:** The reasoning part of an expert system.
- **Kindle:** Amazon’s family of e-readers, first released in 2007.
- **Knowledge base:** The facts and rules of an expert system.
- **Macro:** A recorded set of actions that can be replayed.
- **NAS:** Network Attached Storage on a local network.
- **Perceptual computing:** Computers that sense and understand voice, gesture and faces.
- **Phishing:** Fraudulent messages that trick people into revealing information.

pages.title: P – V
pages.body:
- **Pivot table:** An interactive summary of data.
- **Plug-and-play:** Automatic detection and set-up of new hardware.
- **Pseudocode:** An algorithm written in structured plain English.
- **Ransomware:** Malware that encrypts files and demands payment.
- **Smart card:** A card with a built-in microprocessor chip.
- **Supercomputer:** An extremely fast computer made of thousands of processors.
- **Telemedicine:** Health care delivered at a distance using ICT.
- **Template:** A pre-designed file used as a starting point.
- **Validation:** Rules that control what data can be entered.

pages.title: W
pages.body: - **Wearable display:** A screen worn on the body, e.g. smart glasses or a smartwatch.
